item.title: The Role of Lifestyle in Brain Health: Reducing Risk and Living Well with Dementia
item.description: Dementia is often thought of as an inevitable part of ageing, but this belief is both inaccurate and damaging. While age is a key risk factor, research shows that lifestyle choices play a significant role in brain health and can reduce the risk of developing dementia. For those already living with the condition, these same lifestyle factors can promote better quality of life and slow the progression of symptoms. item.title: Understanding the Early Signs of Dementia: Knowledge is Power
item.description: Dementia is often misunderstood as a natural part of ageing, leading many to overlook the warning signs until the condition has significantly progressed. However, recognising the early symptoms is crucial for obtaining a timely diagnosis, accessing support, and effectively managing the condition. Early intervention not only improves quality of life but also empowers individuals and families to prepare for the future. item.title: From the C Word to the D Word: Breaking the Taboo Around Dementia
item.description: For decades, cancer was known as “the C word” — a term spoken in hushed tones, cloaked in fear and stigma. It carried a dark shadow of secrecy, a diagnosis too heavy to discuss openly in polite company. Those affected by cancer were often left to face it alone, with minimal public understanding or support.But over the years, this secrecy and stigma dissolved. Today, cancer is no longer treated as an unspeakable condition. It is openly discussed, widely researched, and collectively fought against
